name: Dark Orange
lede: Dark Orange is a web color, `darkorange`, a saturated amber orange defined by the hex code FF8C00 in the X11 color set.

sections.title: A web color
sections.body:
Paterson lists DarkOrange among the colors of the X11 color set, with the hex code FF8C00 [1]. The name is a standard label, not a historic one: it is a place on a computer color chart [1].

The swatch is a pure, bright orange, deeper than [[orange]] and more yellow than [[vermilion]]. The phrase dark orange is also used loosely in the books as a plain description, and it names real things in other places.

sections.title: Dark orange in plain words
sections.body:
Paterson defines beeswax as a dark orange, and skyrin as a natural dark orange pigment [2][3]. Pastoureau uses the phrase for russet, the medieval color that fell in status from the twelfth century and became the color of Judas [4]. A reader of the medieval sources should expect that russet leaned toward dark orange and was an insult, not a compliment [4].

Finlay's account of the indigo vat in Bengal records the planter Grant puzzling over the liquid, which was dark orange at first, then light green, then darker green [5]. Fresh indigo liquor looks nothing like its final blue [5]. See [[indigo]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: At FF8C00 almost no painting qualifies: 6 of 23,781 paintings in our archive hold it, about 0.03 per cent [6]. In those it is a highlight color, 83 per cent of its use, as in Cranach's *Adam* of 1528 [6][[painting:commons-Q113465655|Adam]]. The strongest match is an 1830 Kota painting of Maharao Ram Singh II, at 31 per cent of the canvas [6][[painting:cma-314487|Maharao Ram Singh II of Kota]]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a match is a color on a screen, not a pigment test [6].

questions.q: What hex code defines DarkOrange in the X11 color set?
Which medieval figure became the picture of a russet, near dark-orange hair?

openers: Fresh indigo liquor in Bengal was dark orange before it turned green and then blue.
